My call, not the user's. The only match is the toolbar's elevation shadow (0 10px 34px / 0 2px 8px rgba(46,33,112,.16/.08)) — vertically offset, on a LIGHT lilac ground, hue-matched to that ground because neutral black goes muddy over a saturated surface. My call, not the user's. The flagged L188 gradient is .hero-matte-tr: a functional occlusion patch that hides the brand mark baked into the film's closing frames. It is painted in #cbbbe6 — the page's own ground colour, not a chromatic accent — sits on a LIGHT lilac surface, not a dark one, and fades to transparent only so its edge cannot be seen against the film. That is the rule's own prescribed remedy (ground the surface with the background) rather than the decorative glow it targets. Audited every other radial-gradient in the file while triaging: the genuine instance of this pattern was #stories::before, a saturated orange halo washing the dark testimonial section — I deleted it and warmed that section's base ground instead.
